designSummary: Cross-sectional survey with shift-level linkage; prevalence of any missed care and its association with below-plan staffing, adjusted for acuity, with nurses clustered in units.
sampleSize: About 1,150 eligible nurses and a planned response near 50 percent with paid time (c4) give about 575 responses. For overall prevalence near 65 percent with a unit-level design effect of about 2.5, the 95 percent confidence interval is about 6 percentage points either side. For the primary association, about 30 percent of described shifts are expected to be below plan; because the exposure varies within units, the design effect is about 1.3, and 575 responses give about 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 for a 15-point difference (62 against 47 percent). Smaller differences would be estimated with wide intervals.
primaryAnalysis: Mixed-effects logistic regression of any missed care on below-plan shift, with a random intercept for unit, adjusted for acuity, shift type, role, unit type and years of experience; the unadjusted estimate is reported alongside.
secondaryAnalysis: Negative binomial model for the number of activities missed; the same model for missed timed medicines; item-level prevalence by role and shift type, descriptive only.
missingData: Responses without a usable last-shift date cannot be linked and are described separately; item nonresponse above 10 percent is handled by multiple imputation with 20 imputations.
multiplicity: One primary association; secondary outcomes and item-level results are labelled as secondary with confidence intervals only.
software: R with the lme4 package; the analysis plan is lodged with the steering group before the survey opens.
overfittingGuards: No data-driven cut-off for below plan
Cells under five responses suppressed, not merged after looking at results
summary: About 575 responses; about 80 percent power for a 15-point difference after a within-unit design effect of 1.3.
